name: The Object the Vaultborn Answer
summary: The single resonator the sealed population of races.vaultborn draws qi from, held under the extraction guild's charter and described only by those already answering it. It reads as a law imprint held at one value, so it is recorded as resembling one and never as being one. Settle it by observing it from outside its own resonance. If an imprint, the guild's fourth-seat arithmetic becomes lawful; if a source, one group is present twice and the closed budget breaks.

attributes.question: Whether the resonator is one law imprint held at a value, or something that holds qi without being one of the six groups.
attributes.evidence: Every description of it is a resonance report written by a population that has been answering it since birth; no observation exists from outside the answer.
attributes.beneficiary: organizations.quarrywright, because a resonator read as a source keeps the extraction licence and a resonator read as an imprint makes it a fourth-seat claim.
attributes.settlement_test: One description of the object made by somebody who is not a vaultborn and is not drawing qi from it.
attributes.if_settled: An imprint makes the guild's fourth-seat payment a lawful seat; a source means one group is present twice somewhere and the closed six-group supply is not closed.

name: The Register of Unopened Coffins
summary: A mortuary college keeps one sealed case for every death it cannot certify, and the cases accumulate because certifying a death needs a body and the frames keep producing the record without the body. Nothing in the setting has a procedure for a certified death on a frame where life law is seated and spent. The college pays for the seal and charges for the file, so the ambiguity is its standing revenue rather than its failure.

attributes.question: What the frame does to a body that a mortuary college cannot find, and whether the missing body is ever missing or only unfound.
attributes.evidence: A sealed case per uncertified death, each holding a name, a frame, and no verification; the mortuary culture's habit of filing a season late is the same habit taught backward.
attributes.beneficiary: organizations.field_registry, because an unissued certificate is the only instrument it can charge for.
attributes.settlement_test: Open one case and locate its body, or produce one frame where certification succeeds without a body present.
attributes.if_settled: The college either loses its fee and its standing together, or proves that a body can end on a frame whose law cannot describe the ending.

name: The Held-Note Witnesses
summary: The pocket that presses fifteen imprints into one held value admits observers and has returned no two descriptions that agree, so its only surviving record is a list of disagreements. The notary holds the list and certifies none of it, because a certified reading of a fifteen-imprint hold would let a vacant seat be argued filled. Nobody may judge the list: the rule that an office may not judge its own trial is the only reason a witness list survives at all.

attributes.question: What a fifteen-imprint hold actually looks like from inside, given that every observer has returned a different answer.
attributes.evidence: A witness list whose entries disagree pairwise, held unadjudicated by the only office permitted to hold it.
attributes.beneficiary: organizations.nine_seat_notary, and behind it any office whose authority is that a vacancy is not yet proved fillable.
attributes.settlement_test: Two witnesses describing the same instant of the hold, filed together and unredacted.
attributes.if_settled: A single agreed description either certifies the hold as surplus capacity, which collapses the vacancy argument, or proves the pocket is not readable at all, which is worse.

name: The Ward That Agrees With Nothing
summary: A shelf whose frame writes no value matching any neighbour on any group, so the boundary rule has nothing to say about it: nothing can arrive and nothing can leave. The claim over it survives precisely because the agreement a crossing requires can never be produced there. Its holder is therefore the only party in the setting whose title depends on the frame remaining unreachable, and the ward is maintained the way a lock is maintained, by never being opened.

attributes.question: Whether the shelf writes nothing in common by composition, by choice, or because a scar sits where a matching value used to be.
attributes.evidence: No survey has returned from the shelf itself; every account is a claimant describing ground it has not stood on.
attributes.beneficiary: civilizations.fragmentshelf_claim, whose deadline expires on contact, so the ward's value is a function of nobody testing it.
attributes.settlement_test: A frame that writes one matching group, which turns an unreachable ward into a toll.
attributes.if_settled: Either the claim becomes trade, or it becomes a lie with a named holder, and the ward stops being maintained.

name: The Door at Realm Eighteen
summary: The abandoned crossing left a bed of unmortared seats, and something at that bed still answers to a seat nobody has paid for. A monopoly holds the crossing and forbids any sect from holding it, which is a prohibition against a seat being held rather than against a seat existing. Every account of the door closing without a hand describes a seat still paying its own upkeep, and every such account is refused publication.

attributes.question: Whether an unmortared slot can hold an imprint at all, given that a slot is one law written at one value and a bed is not a seat.
attributes.evidence: Repeated reports of a door closing itself, all withdrawn before filing, and a prohibition that names holding rather than existing.
attributes.beneficiary: organizations.bed_of_eighteen, because a door that will not hold a paying holder is a monopoly that cannot be competed for.
attributes.settlement_test: One reading of the bed by somebody who is not the monopoly and is not paying its upkeep.
attributes.if_settled: A seat that pays nothing makes the crossing tariff a payment for nothing and removes the only durable wealth in the setting; a seat that answers nothing makes the bed a monument.

name: Who Pays the Fourth Seat
summary: A pocket cut into a three-seat frame holds four imprints because a warden pays the fourth seat out of their own body once a period, and the payer is not written down anywhere. The extraction guild keeps the payer unnamed because a named payer is a creditor, and a creditor can be repaid and then stopped. So the chamber's fourth seat rests on a subsidy nobody can cite, and the guild's charter describes a fee with no payer.

attributes.question: Whose upkeep funds the fourth seat in a frame whose parent seats three.
attributes.evidence: The seat exists, it persists across periods, and no ledger anywhere carries the payment that must sustain it.
attributes.beneficiary: organizations.quarrywright, for the charter, and organizations.wide_door, which can keep selling passage into a chamber nobody can explain.
attributes.settlement_test: An account naming the payment, in any hand, from anybody who has been inside the chamber.
attributes.if_settled: A named payer makes the fourth seat a claim with an owner; an unnamed one that persists makes it a law reading nothing, which would be worse for everyone.

name: The Ceiling at Realm Seventeen
summary: The densest bodies stop one gate short of the end of their own tier, and the era that produced the stop is the one era with no spare seat to stand outside on. The composition reading and the practice reading make the same prediction from inside a complete composition, so nothing observed so far can separate them. Exactly one account survives, held by a mortuary college that will not corroborate it, because corroboration needs a second body.

attributes.question: Whether realm seventeen is the composition's arithmetic or the practice's habit, given that a complete composition makes both readings identical from inside.
attributes.evidence: One account, from a stonecutter, held unverified by the college that keeps the case.
attributes.beneficiary: The verdict that the mortal ceiling is composed rather than political, because a sibling ceiling at the top of the spirit tier would make every ceiling arguable.
attributes.settlement_test: A dense body at seventeen examined by somebody who is not the examination.
attributes.if_settled: Composed, and the ceiling joins the realm-nine result as arithmetic. Practice, and every ceiling in the setting becomes a policy that somebody chose.

name: The Thirtieth Gate
summary: Bodies holding more life than their frame can inscribe reach the twenty-ninth gate and none has ever come back to describe the thirtieth, so the question is not what is past it but whether past it is a gate or the end of the ladder. No thirty-first is possible in a closed six-group supply, which bounds the question without answering it. The answer is expensive for anyone whose authority depends on the ladder visibly stopping somewhere.

attributes.question: Whether the thirtieth gate is a wall or a terminus, and therefore whether the ladder stops by law or by exhaustion.
attributes.evidence: No return, no description, and a body whose every gate writes a requirement the body cannot satisfy.
attributes.beneficiary: civilizations.star_regent, which holds two tiers and cannot afford the answer being findable, because a top tier is the only thing that makes a lower one worth holding.
attributes.settlement_test: One body past the twenty-ninth that can still report, which the law table says is not possible.
attributes.if_settled: A wall, and the closed six-group supply is complete with a named edge. A terminus, and the top tier's nine vacancies were waiting for a realm that was never printed.

name: The Line Nobody Admits To
summary: A carrier line has no household willing to claim it, and the founding bar it must clear is reachable only by one generation of pure pairing, which is arithmetic rather than history. One household's own record is the oldest surviving evidence and nobody able to disprove it, so the line is old by default rather than by proof. Whether it descends from the culled branches, from the crossings, or from nothing is exactly the question the record cannot answer.

attributes.question: Whether the line descends from the culled branches, from the crossings, or from nothing at all.
attributes.evidence: A single household record, contested by nobody able to disprove it, and a founding bar reachable by exactly one generation of pure pairing.
attributes.beneficiary: organizations.standing_name, the only house whose survival depends on somebody being provably oldest, and organizations.ironpact, whose cull is one of the three candidate origins.
attributes.settlement_test: A second record older than the household's, in any hand, naming a parent.
attributes.if_settled: An origin turns an unfalsifiable default into a claim that can be contested, and the branch cull stops being folklore and starts being a debt.

name: The Payer Nobody Names
summary: The bill for opening a world at all was written in law seats, paid in the only currency with a thousandfold range, and no surviving record names who paid. Every later tier is a receipt for the same payment, so the question is not one omission but the omission at the bottom of a column that runs to the present. A named payer would hold the oldest provable claim in the setting, which is why the highest office does not want one found.

attributes.question: Who paid the first tier's seats, and therefore who owns the only claim in the setting older than every house.
attributes.evidence: Seat-cost curves and a currency named; a payer absent from every record that names the cost.
attributes.beneficiary: politics.office_of_the_star_regent, whose authority is that it inherits an unbroken line; any named payer outranks it.
attributes.settlement_test: Any document contemporaneous with the opening that names a payer rather than a price.
attributes.if_settled: The setting acquires a first creditor, which either ends the current inheritance or proves the founding record is a later reconstruction.

name: The Gauge That Disagrees With Itself
summary: Three surveys of the same anomaly disagree more sharply the longer they are repeated, and disagreement is what makes a certification necessary, so the notary's fee scales with the uncertainty rather than shrinking it. The anomaly is only measurable as distance, and distance requires a seated spatial law the parent frame does not have, so the instrument measures a quantity its frame cannot define. The collapsed pocket is the precedent: every survey since has disagreed more.

attributes.question: Whether the anomaly is a spatial-law scar, an instrument fault, or the tear left where somebody carved fresh rock into a frame with no spatial law.
attributes.evidence: Three survey series whose divergence increases monotonically with the number of surveys, and a collapsed pocket that made every later survey worse.
attributes.beneficiary: organizations.nine_seat_notary, because uncertifiable distance is a standing charge rather than a settled measurement.
attributes.settlement_test: Two instruments, two frames, one reading, or one instrument that survives being carried off the anomaly and still disagrees.
attributes.if_settled: A scar, and the frame once seated spatial law. An instrument fault, and the notary's tariff on this ground is a fraud with a schedule.

name: Why the Tides Stop at the Shore
summary: One tear has stood open long enough to be named, both sides write the same law group at the same value, and no qi tide has ever crossed it. A tide is a law value moving through its range on a cycle, so a cycle that never arrives is the whole content of the question. The shore's liturgy was built on the absence of a mechanism, which is the only kind of rite that cannot be falsified and therefore the only kind that survives a falsification attempt.

attributes.question: Why a standing agreement between two frames produces a passage no cycle uses.
attributes.evidence: An open tear, a matched value, and four centuries of ritual with no measured arrival on the far side.
attributes.beneficiary: cultures.door_liturgy, whose standing rests on there being nothing to explain the rite by.
attributes.settlement_test: A qi value read on the far side at any time, by anyone not part of the shore's rite.
attributes.if_settled: The rite becomes a technique and the shrine's standing collapses, or it becomes a superstition and the shore loses its only lawful reason to exist.

name: The Record Below the Baseline
summary: Strata under the plains carry tool marks that imply a hand, on a frame that seats three law groups and none of them moves distance, so no hand could have worked them. Either the marks predate the current composition, which means the frame was paid for twice, or the frame once seated spatial law and gave it up. The extraction guild's charter rests on the founding record, and both answers destroy it.

attributes.question: Whether the marks predate the frame's present composition, or whether the composition changed after the frame was paid for.
attributes.evidence: Worked faces at a depth below the recorded baseline, and no seated law capable of carrying the work.
attributes.beneficiary: organizations.quarrywright, whose charter is illegitimate under either answer and legitimate under the current record.
attributes.settlement_test: A dated stratum below the marks, or a spatial reading anywhere on the plains that predates the current composition.
attributes.if_settled: A second seam and the iron grief was avoidable, or a forged founding record and every extraction licence on the plains descends from a forgery.

name: The Sixty-Year Gap
summary: The only exact record below the spirit peaks carries sixty years as a summary instead of entry by entry, in a culture whose whole practice is that a count is never an estimate. Compound interest across a gap nobody can audit is either a debt or a forgery, and the difference is the gap. Every house that borrowed across those sixty years is owed an answer it cannot obtain, so the gap is kept legible rather than filled: a filled gap would be an admission.

attributes.question: Whether the summary replaced sixty years of entries or stood in for a settlement nobody recorded.
attributes.evidence: One contiguous summary inside an otherwise exact ledger, at the exact span every borrower claims to have lost paper in.
attributes.beneficiary: Every house whose debt crosses the gap, which is every house old enough to matter.
attributes.settlement_test: Any surviving entry from inside the span, in any hand, agreeing with the summary to the weight standard.
attributes.if_settled: Entries, and sixty years of compound interest is owed. A settlement, and the culture that never estimates has been settling quietly for sixty years.

name: Who Draws Upkeep From the Vacancies
summary: Unclaimed capacity is the only thing that pays its own upkeep, so an unfilled seat is described as funding the tier it sits in. Something is drawing from it, and the budget it draws on is the same closed six groups everything else competes to hold. The notary is paid to certify a seat empty and is the body that would have to certify where the payment went, so the question is administered by its own beneficiary.

attributes.question: What draws upkeep from a seat nothing holds, and whether the draw is a fourteenth law or the seats themselves.
attributes.evidence: A standing tier upkeep with no payer of record, and four immortal plus nine transcendent vacancies nobody may certify empty.
attributes.beneficiary: The transcendent offices, whose entire solvency rests on unclaimed capacity behaving like an asset.
attributes.settlement_test: One period's upkeep traced from an empty seat to a recipient, or an accounting that closes with the seat unfilled and the tier paid.
attributes.if_settled: The seats pay themselves, and every vacancy in the setting is a creditor. The seats are drawn from, and the six groups were never the whole supply.

name: The Walkers Who Never Arrived
summary: A population crossed the stair and neither arrived nor sent word, inside the one movement in the setting with more recorded departures than recorded arrivals. A person who never arrives can be neither charged nor proven dead, so the crossing fee is still held and the crossing has no end. A debt-enforcement house exists because an unclosed crossing is an uncollectable one, so the gap is the firm's standing order rather than a gap in one.

attributes.question: Where a large group went after the stair, and whether anyone arrived who was not on the departure roll.
attributes.evidence: Departure rolls with no arrival column, a fee total that never nets out, and no message in either direction.
attributes.beneficiary: organizations.jade_writ, whose unrecoverable crossing is the reason a debt house exists at all; and every house holding an unclosed fee.
attributes.settlement_test: One body from the roll, alive, or one arrival record naming somebody not on the roll.
attributes.if_settled: They are somewhere, and the fee is owed rather than held. They are not, and the setting has been charging the dead across a toll for four centuries.

name: The One Back From Twenty-Nine
summary: One body returned from the twenty-ninth gate and cannot be examined twice, because the second examination is what the first one prevented. A mortuary college cannot certify dead a body it may not examine, so the survivor stays legally alive indefinitely, owing upkeep indefinitely. An unclosable life and an unclosable seat are the same arrangement read from opposite ends, which is why nobody has tried to close either.

attributes.question: Whether the law table is a hard limit or a set of requirements a body can outgrow, and what a category is for a person who cannot be examined.
attributes.evidence: One return, one refusal of examination, and a name that cannot be struck from any roll.
attributes.beneficiary: organizations.field_registry, which cannot certify the death and therefore keeps certifying the life; and any body that pays per living name.
attributes.settlement_test: One examination performed by a party with no standing to lose, on a copy, in a frame the survivor consents to enter.
attributes.if_settled: A hard limit, and the survivor is the closing evidence. A soft limit, and every ceiling recorded in the setting is a request rather than a composition.

name: The Order Behind the Sixth Seat
summary: The diff that produced the setting's one useful finding kept both readings and kept them privately, and the order that commissioned it is not named. The finding was that surplus seats buy observation rather than new paths, which is the only argument that has ever justified fifteen seats at the top. Its suppression is therefore not tidiness: it decides whether the top tier's slack is a design or an accident, and who inherited it.

attributes.question: Who commissioned the diff, which reading was removed, and whether the top tier's surplus was built or inherited.
attributes.evidence: A method that kept both readings, a finding everyone knows, and no commission anywhere in the record.
attributes.beneficiary: organizations.reckoning_seat, which needs the slack to read as design, because an inherited surplus is an accident somebody else made.
attributes.settlement_test: The commission, or either reading, in a frame outside the top tier's custody.
attributes.if_settled: Design, and the ascendancy court built the composition it rules on. Inherited, and it rules on a structure it did not choose and cannot justify.

name: The Clause Cut From the Ledger
summary: The passage ledger records a central prohibition, that a seat may not be levied, and records nothing about the last time somebody levied one. A prohibition with no recorded violation is a prohibition with no enforcement, so the setting's central economic rule may be a sentence rather than a fact. The vacancy office exists to certify that nothing was taken, which is only worth doing if taking was once attempted.

attributes.question: Whether levying a seat was ever attempted, and what happened to whoever tried.
attributes.evidence: A prohibition in the ledger's own words and no case law, no record, and no precedent anywhere.
attributes.beneficiary: The marshal's office, whose authority over the crossings descends from the prohibition and would descend from a refusal instead if one had been recorded.
attributes.settlement_test: Any finding, fine, or execution naming a levied seat, from any tier's record.
attributes.if_settled: An enforcement record makes the rule a fact with a date. Nothing, and the tariff is a payment for a service the setting has never been owed.

name: The Surplus of the Held Note
summary: Fifteen imprints pressed into one held value leaves nine readings with nothing written in them, and the pocket does something with them that no witness agrees on. The closed budget permits exactly one reading of that: stored. A mind path that claims a self can be sustained past the end of any civilisation only needs the hold to be a resource rather than a posture, which is why nobody asks.

attributes.question: Whether the nine unwritten readings are stored, or are a source the six-group budget does not admit.
attributes.evidence: A composition with nine surplus imprints, and a witness list in which no two entries describe the same use.
attributes.beneficiary: cosmology.mind_dao, whose central claim needs the hold to be storable rather than merely sustainable.
attributes.settlement_test: One witness describing what a slot does when nothing is written in it, corroborated by an instrument rather than a body.
attributes.if_settled: Storage, and the top tier has a battery. A source, and the closed six-group supply has three unlisted branches.

name: The Third Elemental Department
summary: Three attempts were made to seat elemental law in a spirit-tier frame; the record keeps one name and drops the other two. The law census already names three groups as never installed and keeps their names, so whether two of them were seated and then unseated is not a cosmetic question. It decides whether absence has a fourth signature, which is a revision to the rule that gives absence exactly three.

attributes.question: Whether two of the three elemental attempts were seated and unseated, or never written at all.
attributes.evidence: One surviving department name, two dropped, and a census that retained the names of laws it recorded as never installed.
attributes.beneficiary: Whoever holds the surviving name's descendants, and any office whose standing depends on absence having only three forms.
attributes.settlement_test: Either dropped name in a frame that seated it, or in any record of an unseating.
attributes.if_settled: Never seated, and the census is complete. Seated and unseated, and absence by decision is a fourth signature, which rewrites the rule rather than the record.

name: Whether the River Still Runs
summary: A river is a clock on any frame, and the frame the plains sit on left temporal law unwritten, so nothing down there should be able to keep time. Either the water moves on qi at the floor value, in which case the flow is a law reading rather than a current, or it has not moved since the frame was paid for. The frame that bought a calendar with its ability to be alive is the control case: same absence, opposite purchase.

attributes.question: Whether the flow is a law reading at the floor value or a current, and whether the river is running now.
attributes.evidence: A channel cut to a shape no floor value makes, a silt line nobody dates, and an hour-keeping culture whose hours nothing downstream can verify.
attributes.beneficiary: cultures.quiet_hour, which keeps hours the plains cannot check, so the river is its only clock and its stillness is a liturgy problem rather than a hydrology one.
attributes.settlement_test: One measurement of the same standing mark in two seasons, by somebody who is not keeping an hour.
attributes.if_settled: Running, and the plains has a clock it never paid for. Still, and every hour kept in the time culture is a local fiction with a liturgy attached.

name: The Wake That Did Not Claim
summary: An ectospecies body returns to its own door and does not enter, and nobody has ever recorded what happens on the threshold. The threshold faith is defined by what it does not admit, so a refusal is the rite running exactly as designed, and the builders' marks measure something that may never have been theirs to set. The question is whether the door is a rite or a law, and a faith cannot ask it without losing the ground it stands on.

attributes.question: Whether the door's refusal is a rite the survivors perform or a law the door holds.
attributes.evidence: Repeated refusals at the same doors, no admission anywhere, and no record of what the marks were measured against.
attributes.beneficiary: cultures.door_liturgy, whose entire position is that the threshold is not a mechanism anybody can operate.
attributes.settlement_test: One door marked by the builders that admits a wake, in a frame with no rite performed at it.
attributes.if_settled: A rite, and the survivors are refusing something they could stop refusing. A law, and the oldest surviving technique on the ground is the oldest surviving error.

name: The Three Masters of the First Breath
summary: Three names are attached to the first fuel rationing and no two records place them in the same place on the same day. The master's title first appears one event after the census that required it, which is late enough for a title to be created and early enough for a person to be given it. An office whose legitimacy is that it began the count cannot afford three people beginning it, so the disagreement is kept as a disagreement.

attributes.question: Whether the first ration had one author or three, and whether the office or the person came first.
attributes.evidence: Three names, no shared location record, and a title whose first appearance postdates the census that created the job.
attributes.beneficiary: organizations.nine_seat_notary, and every office whose authority is that it began something.
attributes.settlement_test: One document placing two of the three in one place, or the title's first appearance dated before the census.
attributes.if_settled: One, and every founding claim in the setting is a sole origin. Three, and the first count was a collaboration, which dissolves the word first from every office that owns it.

name: The Roll of the Absent
summary: A levy company is paid per name and keeps a roll of people who were levied and neither returned nor were recorded dead, so the roll grows and nothing on it closes. It is the walked gap written in the wrong register, and the two have never been added up because neither office reads the other's column. A levy that cannot be closed is the only line item in the setting that never needs closing.

attributes.question: Whether the absent are unlocated, undeclared, or simply never written off, and which office holds the other column.
attributes.evidence: A roll with no closure column, a levy total that has never been reconciled, and no death certificate for any name on it.
attributes.beneficiary: organizations.ninth_watch, whose pay scales with the size of an open roll rather than with any recovery.
attributes.settlement_test: One name struck from the roll by a process that does not first require the roll to shrink.
attributes.if_settled: They are somewhere, and a levy company has been funding an expedition for a generation. They are not, and the company has been paid for the dead across a frontier nobody manned.

name: Whether a Seat Can Be Declined
summary: The rule is that the highest office may name a seat and may not take one, and there is no procedure for a seat offered and refused. A vacancy with no refusal procedure can only be filled by acceptance, which is why the notary certifies vacancy and never availability. One perpetuity survives only because its holder was never actually offered anything, so the setting has never seen a refusal recorded.

attributes.question: What a seat does when it is offered to somebody who says no, and whether that refusal is a right or an impossibility.
attributes.evidence: One office forbidden to self-appoint, one notary certifying vacancy only, and no form anywhere for declining.
attributes.beneficiary: organizations.nine_seat_notary, because availability is a thing with a form and a declined seat is a thing with a witness.
attributes.settlement_test: One recorded offer and one recorded refusal, in any office's hand.
attributes.if_settled: A right, and every vacancy becomes an offer that somebody turned down, which converts unclaimed capacity into refused capacity. An impossibility, and the perpetuity is the only refusal in the setting because it was engineered.

name: The Count Below the Stair
summary: Audible reports of a rhythm from under the stair, at a rate nobody reproduces, whose periodicity only matches the mortal realm ladder if time is running at its floor value. A frame at the qi floor has almost nothing to run on, so a count that keeps time is close to the most a mortal composition can be doing. An asymptote culture needs a limit that never arrives, and a rhythm arriving from underneath is the most useful kind.

attributes.question: What is counting in mortal time units underneath a stair that removes people from mortal time.
attributes.evidence: A periodicity reproducible only by ear, never by instrument, and a match to the ladder's spacing at the authored floor value.
attributes.beneficiary: cultures.deadroad, whose asymptote requires a boundary that recedes; and anyone who would rather the rhythm were not measured.
attributes.settlement_test: One instrument that holds the count across two visits, or a resonance recorded by anything other than a witness.
attributes.if_settled: A mechanism, and the floor value is running something. An echo, and the most persistent report on the stair is the one the stair produces itself.

name: The One Child Who Was Filed
summary: Inside a paperless people there is exactly one filed child, and the hand that wrote the record is not one the culture writes. The frame is named unwritable, and a readable record inside it makes the name a claim rather than a description, which is a worse thing to be governed by than a censor. A residue broker pays for legible residue, so the only party that wants the hand read is the one that must not learn it can be.

attributes.question: Who wrote the record, and whether the frame is unwritable or merely unreadable to the people inside it.
attributes.evidence: One readable entry, a hand no local writes, and a culture that has kept it unread for four centuries without explaining why.
attributes.beneficiary: cultures.unfiled, who can deny any debt while no record in their reach is legible; organizations.salt_leech, who would pay for the residue.
attributes.settlement_test: The hand compared against any surviving sample, by a party with no claim on the result.
attributes.if_settled: Foreign, and the paperless people are not what they say they are. Native, and the frame writes records into hands, which means unwritable was always the wrong word for it.

name: The Frame That Agrees and Nothing Crosses
summary: Two frames write one group at one value and have done so as long as anyone recorded, and nothing has crossed in either direction. Every crossing in the setting shares a group with a live neighbour, so this pair satisfies the boundary rule completely and still has no passage, which no name in the setting covers. If adjacency is as cheap as the rule says, the crossing tariff is a tax on nothing and every house on the ladder is built on it.

attributes.question: Whether a standing matched agreement produces no passage because nothing has been sent, or because one side's self-report of its own value can be false.
attributes.evidence: A matched value in both frames' own records, no crossing in either direction, and no route, toll, or refusal anywhere.
attributes.beneficiary: Every house whose standing rests on a crossing tariff, and any office whose authority is a permission no agreement has exercised.
attributes.settlement_test: One body sent across a matched agreement by a party that gains nothing from the transit.
attributes.if_settled: Sending works, and passage is cheap and the tariff is a fiction. One report is false, and a frame's own account of its law values can be forged, which no seal in the setting tests.

name: The Heresy With a Test Site
summary: The form-only reading, form winning with physical law alone where qi is already spent, was recorded as a heresy because nothing in a three-slot frame can test it. The immortal frame holds four duplicate seats, which is exactly the surplus a diff needs, so somewhere the test was possible. No result is recorded, and a tested heresy is a second school competing for the same seats, so the absence of a result is the most stable fact about it.

attributes.question: Whether the form-only claim was ever diffed on a frame with surplus seats, and what the diff said.
attributes.evidence: A duplicate-seat composition that could hold the test, an unpublished claim, and no result in any record.
attributes.beneficiary: organizations.gap_school, which teaches the claim as a heresy because a tested heresy would be a rival school competing for the same seats.
attributes.settlement_test: One diff of form-only against full composition on a frame with a spare seat, in any hand.
attributes.if_settled: Untested, and the body path's confinement was a measurement failure three ages deep. Tested, and the result was suppressed by whichever reading lost.

name: The Account Paid in Iron
summary: An account, held with continuous custody, that the opening payment was made in ore rather than in qi, because ore is the only dense material the plains produce and an ore debt needs no invented currency. The ledger says qi, on the grounds that only qi has a thousandfold range. The disagreement is the record: which currency opened the world decides whether the iron grief was a shortage or a repayment that came due.

attributes.claim: The first tier's seats were paid in ore, and the qi figure is a later rationalisation of an ore debt.
attributes.custody: Unbroken, which is the account's whole strength and the reason it is taught rather than proven.
attributes.evidence: A continuous ore ledger reaching back before the first census, and a qi figure with no early witness.
attributes.beneficiary: organizations.ironpact, whose founding claim is an ore debt and which wants the ore account to be the true one.
attributes.settlement_test: A contemporaneous record naming a currency, or an ore ledger that stops before the first census rather than at it.
attributes.if_settled: Iron, and the iron grief was a repayment schedule that ran out on schedule. Qi, and the ore ledger is a later fiction with a very old date on it.

name: The Account Paid in Qi
summary: The ledger's own reading: qi is the only law with a thousandfold range, so it is the only currency that could fund a tier, and the payer is unnamed because a payer who could be named would still exist. The account has no custodian, which is why it is always the second version and always the better sourced one. It is also the only reading under which the later ascension was irreversible rather than merely attractive.

attributes.claim: The first tier's seats were paid in qi, and the ore account is an ore debt read backwards through a later scarcity.
attributes.custody: None, which is why the challenge is always better sourced and always loses.
attributes.evidence: The authored seat-cost curve, the thousandfold range of the qi law, and an unnamed payer consistent with a payment nobody could inherit.
attributes.beneficiary: The offices that inherit an unbroken authority from a payer nobody can name.
attributes.settlement_test: A contemporaneous record naming a currency, or an early witness to the payment itself.
attributes.if_settled: Qi, and every later tier is a receipt for the same payment. Iron, and the founding record was reconstructed by people who did not own the ore.

name: The Account That the Seam Ran Out
summary: The grief is arithmetic: the mortal tier's only caging ore ran out at the seam, and a frame with no seated spatial law cannot open fresh rock, so one exhausted seam cost the tier its whole ladder. The account is the taught one and is uncontested by anybody with standing, which is precisely why it has never been tested against a claim. It is also the account that makes the ascent an economic migration rather than a forced one.

attributes.claim: The seam was exhausted and the absent spatial law made it impossible to open another, so the grief was arithmetic.
attributes.custody: The taught version, held by everybody and therefore by nobody in particular.
attributes.evidence: An exhausted working face and no seated spatial law, both consistent with the frame and with a closure.
attributes.beneficiary: Every cultivator who climbed out of the grief and every house whose fortune dates from the ascent.
attributes.settlement_test: A sealed face with tool marks younger than the exhaustion, or a licence naming whoever held the seam.
attributes.if_settled: Depletion, and the tier was starved by arithmetic. Sealing, and a population was moved by decision and the ascent was not economic.

name: The Account That the Seam Was Sealed
summary: The competing account: the seam was closed by whoever held the mining charter, and the missing spatial law is not the cause but the reason nobody could reopen it and therefore the reason it stayed closed. The one later attempt to open fresh rock tore the parent frame, which is what a closed seam looks like when somebody tries it again. The guild teaches this version because a depleted seam is a tragedy and a sealed one is a licence somebody still holds.

attributes.claim: The seam was sealed under a charter and the absent spatial law is what kept it sealed, not what emptied it.
attributes.custody: Held by the extraction guild, which benefits from a closure and is the only body with both the claim and the seam.
attributes.evidence: A carved pocket that tore its parent frame, a charter with no expiry, and no dated exhaustion.
attributes.beneficiary: organizations.quarrywright, whose licence is a closure; and any house that profited from the departure the closure caused.
attributes.settlement_test: A licence naming a holder, or tool marks at the sealed face younger than the working face behind it.
attributes.if_settled: Sealed, and the grief was a decision with a beneficiary and the ascent a forced migration. Depleted, and the guild has been holding a closure it did not make.

name: The Account That the Cull Saved the Line
summary: The clan's own version: the branch cull preserved a lineage that debt was about to end, and concentration inside one household was the only way the grant survived at all. It is the oldest account and the only one with an unbroken custody chain, because the clan kept it. The version is preserved by the people it flatters, which is the entire dispute: the same cull is described by its survivors as rescue.

attributes.claim: The cull preserved a line that cultivation debt would otherwise have ended, and the concentration was rescue rather than selection.
attributes.custody: The clan's own record, continuous, and the reason the account survives while its rival is only ever repeated.
attributes.evidence: A narrowed line that still cultivates, and a grant that favours sustained effort over sudden effort.
attributes.beneficiary: organizations.ironpact, which holds a merit under the rescue reading and a debt under the other.
attributes.settlement_test: A branch outside the cull that carries the same grant, which would show the line was found rather than made.
attributes.if_settled: Rescue, and the cull is a debt paid well. Selection, and the clan chose the trait it now claims to have preserved.

name: The Account That the Cull Made the Line
summary: The challenger's version: debt selects for sustained effort, the cull selected for it hardest, and the line's grant is therefore a description of the selection rather than of the blood. No party keeps this account, which is why it is always second and always better sourced than the one that is kept. It is also the only reading under which the unowned genealogy becomes resolvable, because it supplies the third origin.

attributes.claim: The cull manufactured the line by selecting under debt for exactly the trait the grant now describes.
attributes.custody: None; it survives as field-culture practice and in no archive.
attributes.evidence: The grant's shape, the debt that caused the cull, and a founding bar reachable by one generation of pure pairing.
attributes.beneficiary: The unowned genealogy, whose third origin this is; and any house that would rather not owe restitution.
attributes.settlement_test: A pre-cull branch carrying the same sustained-effort grant at the same rate.
attributes.if_settled: Manufactured, and the line is a policy four centuries old wearing a bloodline. Saved, and the challenger's account is a plausible reading of arithmetic that nobody can complete.

name: The Account That the Ledger Frame Was Torn
summary: The taught account: the frame's qi was driven past the top of its range by a trade, the group stopped holding, and the tear it opened met a world it agreed with on nothing. An injury produces refugees, so this version predicts a scattered people. It cannot explain four centuries of paperless practice, which is a settlement with a date rather than a wound.

attributes.claim: The frame was torn by driving its qi past the top of its range, and everything downstream is displacement.
attributes.custody: The taught version, held by nobody with standing to be harmed by the alternative.
attributes.evidence: A frame whose tear met nothing it agreed with, and a trade that moved qi past its range.
attributes.beneficiary: The paperless people, who are described as refugees and therefore as having arrived from somewhere rather than as owing anything.
attributes.settlement_test: A dated interruption in the frame's agreement with itself, or a qi reading above its authored range from any period.
attributes.if_settled: Torn, and the people are displaced and the frame owes them a route home. A choice, and the oldest continuous practice in the setting has an author.

name: The Account That the Ledger Frame Stopped Paying
summary: The challenger's account: the frame's qi was never driven, it was withheld, and the frame stopped paying its own upkeep and therefore stopped agreeing with anything. A decision produces a practice, which is what four centuries of abandoning a price list looks like, and a decision produces a debt. Nobody inside the frame can corroborate it, because the only record is the one the frame cannot write.

attributes.claim: The frame stopped paying its own upkeep, stopped agreeing with anything as a result, and has been unwritten on purpose ever since.
attributes.custody: The paperless people teach it to their children, which is why the version nobody can corroborate is the one everybody inside it can state.
attributes.evidence: An abandoned price list with a date, a mutual-guarantee house founded because the frame could not be written down and then could not be reached, and one readable record inside the whole.
attributes.beneficiary: cultures.unfiled, whose lineage claim is only available under this reading; and whoever withheld the payment.
attributes.settlement_test: A qi reading inside its authored range from any period after the practice began, or the account of the payment itself.
attributes.if_settled: A choice, and the paperless people are descendants of a decision rather than of a wound, and their unrecordability is a privilege with an author. A tear, and they are refugees who have stopped moving for four centuries.

name: The Seventh Ward, Never Built
summary: The taught account, and the reason the name survives as a record rather than a place: a slot was spent on a law that was never defined, the absence consumed it, and thereafter a vacant slot cannot be told from an empty one. It is the safer reading because it leaves the six-group supply closed and the upper vacancies surplus. It is taught by every office whose authority depends on a vacancy being unprovable.

attributes.claim: The seventh ward was never built: the slot was spent on an undefined law and cannot now be distinguished from an empty one.
attributes.custody: Every office that certifies vacancy, all of whom would be dissolved by the alternative.
attributes.evidence: A name kept as a record rather than a place, and a slot that reads empty without ever having been certified empty.
attributes.beneficiary: Any authority that cannot act without a vacancy it cannot certify, and the notary above all of them.
attributes.settlement_test: Any residue of an imprint that was once written in that slot, or any frame whose composition shows a seventh group.
attributes.if_settled: Never built, and the closed six-group supply is complete with a named edge and nothing more. Built, and the supply is curated, which is a different universe.

name: The Seventh Ward, Built and Unseated
summary: The forbidden account: something was seated in that slot, held long enough to be written and paid for, and was later unseated, which would make the six-group supply not closed but curated by whoever could afford to remove a group. A residue broker trades in what a removed imprint leaves behind, so this account has a customer. If it is right, the nine vacancies at the top were manufactured and the tier's upkeep is being paid out of a hole somebody dug.

attributes.claim: A seventh group was seated in that slot, held for a period, and removed, so the supply is curated rather than closed.
attributes.custody: None, which is why it survives only as residue prices and never as a reading.
attributes.evidence: A held pocket where fifteen imprints are pressed into one value, and a residue market that has never explained what it is trading.
attributes.beneficiary: organizations.salt_leech, who needs a removed imprint to have existed; and anyone who profited from the removal.
attributes.settlement_test: One frame whose composition shows a group outside the six, or a residue lot whose origin cannot be dated to a removal.
attributes.if_settled: Built and lost, and the upper vacancies were made rather than found, so the setting's central scarcity is a policy. Never built, and the residue market has been trading in a slot for four centuries.

name: The Account That the Cutaway Isle Is a Copy
summary: The taught account: a spirit isle was cut from the shelf's floor when a jade seam was worked out from under it and resealed with the same six groups at drifted readings, so a severed piece keeps its laws and slowly stops agreeing with its parent. It is the only reading consistent with a seam worked from underneath. It cannot explain why the isle's jade reads at a number nobody ashore can match.

attributes.claim: The isle is a severed piece of the shelf, resealed at drifted readings, and its jade drifted with the frame.
attributes.custody: The shore's own account, held by everybody who has a claim on the seam and by nobody who has stood on the isle.
attributes.evidence: A seam worked out from under the isle, six groups resealed, and a reading that no survey from the parent can match.
attributes.beneficiary: Every house holding a shore claim, since a copy is derived and a parent is original.
attributes.settlement_test: A parent-frame reading matching the isle's jade within one survey's tolerance.
attributes.if_settled: A copy, and the isle's people are a colony and their jade is the shelf's to ration. A body, and the ration has been cut from a supply nobody owns.

name: The Account That the Cutaway Isle Is Its Own Frame
summary: The challenger's account: the isle was never part of the shelf, and it was shaped to look severed, which is why its jade reads at a number no shore survey can match because it was never at the shore's number. A frame that never joined a parent cannot drift from one, so the isle's population are not a colony and the jade was never anybody's to ration. The account has no custodian and one very strong physical detail.

attributes.claim: The isle is a frame in its own right, shaped to resemble a severance, and its jade was never the shelf's.
attributes.custody: None; it is the version the isle's own people tell and the shore does not record.
attributes.evidence: A jade reading unreachable from any shore survey, and an isle whose laws have drifted in a direction severance does not predict.
attributes.beneficiary: The isle's own population, whose only claim to their ground is that it was never anyone else's.
attributes.settlement_test: Any parent-frame measurement within a factor of the isle's reading, or an isle record predating the working of the seam.
attributes.if_settled: A body, and the jade ration is a tax on a supply with no holder and the isle's people are not colonists. A copy, and the shore has been rationing somebody else's jade on its own authority.
